title: async comm/compute interleaving with KV-coalescer for tensor-parallel stages
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Improves multi-GPU tensor-parallel throughput by enabling NCCL collectives to run on dedicated communication streams with compute/comm overlap, and adds a KV cache coalescer to reduce small all-reduce frequency. Typical throughput uplift: 8-15% depending on sequence length and batch shape.
description:
Summary: This PR introduces a coordinated runtime change that interleaves NCCL collectives with compute on dedicated CUDA streams and adds a KV-cache coalescer that batches small KV updates across micro-batches. The goal is to reduce host-side stalls and small-message overhead in tensor-parallel workloads so multi-GPU serving latency and throughput are both improved without changing model semantics.

Motivation and context: Several customer workloads and internal benchmarks showed repetitive small all-reduce calls from the KV cache hot-path causing NCCL enqueue latency and host synchronization in TP stages (see ENG-1729). Existing batcher improvements helped for large batches but left micro-batch shapes and streaming inference with short sequences exposed. This PR targets the runtime overlap and message coalescing layer rather than model code to keep changes backward-compatible.

What changed (high-level):
- Added comm stream abstraction at runtime: NCCL collectives launched on a dedicated comm stream with lightweight CUDAEvent fences to overlap with compute stream progress.
- Implemented KVCacheCoalescer: buffers KV-shard updates across N micro-batches (configurable window) and issues a single coalesced all-reduce when safe. Coalescer respects strict consistency for pinned checkpoints and can be disabled per model.
- Scheduler changes: new "tp_overlap" scheduling policy that slices tensor-parallel steps into compute chunks and issues prefetch/collectives earlier to maximize overlap. Policy falls back to previous linear scheduling when hardware topology lacks P2P or when comm streams are not supported.
- Kernel wrapper updates: small wrappers to ensure NCCL ops are launched without implicit device synchronization and with explicit stream affinity.
- Deterministic ordering: event-based ordering to preserve deterministic outputs for the same seed/input, verified by added determinism tests.
- Perf harness and tests: added tp_overlap_e2e.py microbenchmark and a regression test that runs constrained small-batch shapes to catch regressions in coalescing logic.

Commits (summary):
- commit 9a3b7d3 — runtime: add comm-stream abstraction and helpers
- commit 2b8f1c4 — tp: implement tp_overlap scheduler policy and config toggle
- commit f4d2e8a — kv: implement KVCacheCoalescer and config knobs
- commit 6c12ab1 — tests: add tp_overlap_e2e and determinism regression suite
- commit d9b3f21 — ci: add nccl-integration job and flakiness mitigations

Files (changed, high-level):
- runtime/comm/comm_stream.h, runtime/comm/comm_stream.cpp — comm stream impl, events, and helpers
- runtime/scheduler/tp_overlap_scheduler.cpp — new scheduling policy and orchestration hooks
- runtime/kv/kv_coalescer.h, runtime/kv/kv_coalescer.cpp — coalescing logic and metrics
- runtime/benchmarks/tp_overlap_e2e.py — microbenchmark for throughput/latency measurement
- tests/regression/test_kv_coalesce_determinism.py — deterministic checks for coalescer
- ci/.github/workflows/nccl-integration.yml — new integration job that runs a small multi-node NCCL smoke matrix
- docs/runtime/notes/tp-overlap.md — internal design note and config knobs
- examples/tp/README.md — usage and how to enable tp_overlap in config

Backward compatibility: KVCacheCoalescer can be disabled via model config (kv.coalesce_window=0) and tp_overlap policy is opt-in. Default coalescing window is conservative (2 micro-batches) and auto-tunes based on observed latency in the first N steps. If topology lacks P2P or the driver reports unsupported streams, we fall back to legacy scheduling.

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks run on a 8xA100 (80GB) node and a 4xA100 instance with TP=4 shard setup:
- Baseline (main) median throughput: 1000 tokens/s
- This PR median throughput: 1108 tokens/s (+10.8%) for short sequences (<=256) and small micro-batches
- Long sequences (2048) saw smaller gains (~6-8%) since batching already amortizes reductions.
- Tail latency remained within 5% of baseline; p95 latency slightly improved in most shapes.

Risk and mitigations:
- Race conditions with events: added robust tests and a conservative retry path to reissue collectives if event ordering validated failure is detected.
- Topology edge cases: explicit fallback to legacy scheduler for non-P2P or NVLink-less topologies.
- Determinism: added deterministic unit tests and long-run smoke tests on CI.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Riley Chen (review): "Nice separation between comm stream and scheduler. Two requests: 1) add a safety check for driver versions that don't support external stream NCCL launches; 2) add a flag to force coalescer off for hotfix rollouts."
- Author (Asha): "Added driver version gating and model config flag (kv.coalesce_force_off). Documented both in docs/runtime/notes/tp-overlap.md."
- Marcel Dupont (review): "Observed a flaky failure on CI: nccl-integration sometimes hangs when coalescer window=1 under extreme synthetic load. Also, please ensure we don't increase GPU memory beyond expectations."
- Author (Asha): "Fixed the hang by enforcing an explicit cudaEventRecord before issuing comm ops; also added a memory ceiling check in the coalescer and an evict path if memory threshold exceeded. Updated tests to cover window=1."
- Lina Ortega (approval): "Verified deterministic outputs on 3 seeds and perf uplift on our internal suites; good to merge once CI passes."

CI status and iteration:
- Initial run: failed on nccl-integration (hang) and one lint warning.
- After event fence fix and memory ceiling: rerun, nccl-integration passed; full suite green.
- Final status: all checks passed (unit, integration, perf smoke).

Merge decision: Squash-merged to main after approvals. Rollout plan: feature gated by runtime config flag (scheduler.tp_policy=\"tp_overlap\") and kv.coalesce_window default is conservative. We will enable for a subset of Dedicated customers and monitor token-level metrics (cost/latency) and determinism traces for a week before broader rollout (see ENG-1984).

Notes for on-call/operations:
- If serving jobs experience repeated NCCL stalls after enabling, set kv.coalesce_force_off=true and scheduler.tp_policy=\"legacy\" as immediate mitigation.
- Telemetry: new metrics added: runtime.comm.overlap_percent, runtime.kv.coalesce_rate, runtime.comm.event_waits. Alerts will be created in a follow-up PR if rollout shows abnormal regressions.

Related PRs/Work items: ENG-1729 (investigation), ENG-1984 (rollout plan), follow-up will include adaptive coalescing thresholds based on latency targets.

Author commits and sign-off: Asha Patel — implemented changes, wrote tests, fixed CI flakes. Approved by Riley Chen and Lina Ortega. Merged by Marcel Dupont.

This PR should help multi-GPU TP serving workloads achieve better throughput on small-batch/short-sequence streaming inference by reducing small-collective overhead and exposing more overlap between comm and compute.
